Content: Editor's note: The test requirements in this section refer explicitly to Category M1, but they are also applicable to Category M2 and non-BL CE UEs. Pending discussion in RAN4 is needed to update the wording. When the UE receives a RRC message implying handover the UE shall finish the transmission of all repetitions of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command, Where: D equals the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in 3GPP TS 36.331 plus the interruption time stated in clause 5.5.2.1.2. The interruption time is the time between the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command on the old PDSCH and the moment the UE has transmitted all repetitions of PRACH in the target cell, excluding the RRC procedure delay. This requirement applies when UE is not required to perform any synchronisation procedure before transmitting on the new PRACH. When intra-frequency handover or inter-frequency handover is commanded and the field sameSFN-Indication and mib-RepetitionStatus are included in the handover command then the interruption time shall be less than T interrupt T interrupt = T + T + 20 ms When intra-frequency handover or inter-frequency handover is commanded and the field sameSFN-Indication or mib-RepetitionStatus is not included in the handover command then UE the interruption time shall be less than T interrupt T interrupt = T + T + T + 20 ms Where: T is the time required to search the target cell when the handover command is received by the UE. If the target cell is known, then T = 0 ms. If the target cell is unknown and signal quality is sufficient for successful cell detection on the first attempt, then T = 80 ms. Otherwise, T shall be according to the non-DRX cell identification requirements specified in Clause 8.13.2.1 for intra-frequency handover for a UE configured with CEModeA or T shall be according to the non-DRX cell identification requirements specified in Clause 8.13.2.6 for inter-frequency handover for a UE configured with CEModeA. Regardless of whether DRX is in use by the UE, T shall still be based on non-DRX target cell search times. T is the time required for acquiring the MIB information of the target cell. T is the time required to complete the transmission of PRACH in the target cell. The actual value of T shall depend upon the uncertainty in acquiring the first available PRACH occasion based on the PRACH configuration used in the target cell and the PRACH coverage enhancement level used by the UE for sending the random access preamble to the target cell. In the interruption requirement a cell is known if it has been meeting the relevant cell identification requirement for a time duration equal or longer than the time duration required for the cell identification. Otherwise, it is unknown. For intra-frequency handover the time duration required for the cell identification is specified in relevant intra-frequency cell identification requirements as described in Clause 8.13.2.1 for CEModeA. For inter-frequency handover the time duration required for the cell identification is specified in relevant inter-frequency cell identification requirements as described in Clause 8.13.2.6 for CEModeA. Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN HD-FDD inter frequency handover for CE UEs in CEModeA > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. PDCCHs indicating new transmissions shall be sent continuously to ensure that the UE would not enter the DRX state. The test consists of three successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2 and T3 respectively. At the start of time duration T1, the UE may not have any timing information of Cell 2. Starting T2, Cell 2 becomes detectable and the UE is expected to detect and send a measurement report. The start of T3 is defined as the end of the last TTI containing the RRC message implying handover. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF-CE according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3AA. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.28.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1. T1 starts. The SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.28.5-1. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table H.3.2-3 implying handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRCConnectionReconfiguration message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power setting from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.28.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE finishes the transmission of all repetitions of the PRACH to Cell 2 less than 170 ms from the beginning of time period T3 then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. After T3 expires, cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF-CE according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3AA. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat steps 2-12 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

NOTE: The handover delay can be expressed as: RRC procedure delay + T , where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in 3GPP TS 36.331. T = 120 + 35 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.5.2.1.2 in 3GPP TS 36.133. This gives a total of 170 ms.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The purpose of DAPS handover is to change the PCell to another cell. A DAPS handover is synchronous if it meets the conditions in Table 5.1.41.3-1, otherwise it is asynchronous. Procedure delays for the procedure that can command a DAPS handover are specified in TS 36.331 . DAPS delay is comprised of D and D . When the UE receives an RRC message implying handover, the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command when UE is configured with dual active protocol stack handover. D = T + T + T + 20 ms Where T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is the time required to search the target cell when the target cell is not already known when the handover command is received by the UE. If the target cell is known, then T = 0 ms. If the target cell is unknown and signal quality is sufficient for successful cell detection on the first attempt, then T = 80 ms. Regardless of whether DRX is in use by the UE, T shall still be based on non-DRX target cell search times. T is the interruption uncertainty in acquiring the first available PRACH occasion in the new cell. T can be up to 30 ms. NOTE: The actual value of T shall depend upon the PRACH configuration used in the target cell. A cell is known if it has been meeting the relevant cell identification requirement during the last 5 seconds otherwise it is unknown. Relevant cell identification requirements are described in TS 36.133 Clause 8.1.2.2.1 (FDD) and TS 36.133 Clause 8.1.2.2.2 (TDD) for intra-frequency handover and TS 36.133 Clause 8.1.2.3.1 (FDD) and TS 36.133 Clause 8.1.2.3.2 (TDD) for inter-frequency handover. After successful RACH procedure of the target cell, when the UE receives an RRC message implying source cell release command, the UE shall accomplish the release actions specified in TS 36.331 within D . D = T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is defined in TS 36.133 clause 5.7.2.1.2. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on source cell: T is 1 ms for synchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover and 2ms for asynchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover, when the bandwidth of target cell is no larger than the bandwidth of source cell, T is 2ms for synchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover and 3ms for asynchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover, when the bandwidth of target cell is larger than the bandwidth of source cell, T is 5 ms for synchronous intra-band inter-frequency DAPS handover and 6 ms for asynchronous intra-band inter-frequency DAPS handover T is 1 ms for synchronous inter-band inter-frequency DAPS handover and 2 ms for asynchronous inter-band inter-frequency DAPS handover. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on target cell: T is 2 ms for synchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover and 3 ms for asynchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover, when the bandwidth of target cell is smaller than the bandwidth of source cell. T is 1 ms for synchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover and 2 ms for asynchronous intra-frequency DAPS handover, when the bandwidth of target cell is not smaller than the bandwidth of source cell T is 5 ms for synchronous intra-band inter-frequency DAPS handover and 6 ms for asynchronous intra-band inter-frequency DAPS handover. T is 1 ms for synchronous inter-band inter-frequency DAPS handover and 2ms for asynchronous inter-band inter-frequency DAPS handover. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.7.1, 5.7.2.1 and A.5.1.41.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in TS 36.508 Annex A figure A.14 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.78a for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set up according to Table 5.1.41.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Message contents are defined in clause 5.1.41.4.3. There are two E-UTRA TDD carriers and two cells on that carrier specified in the test. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test. 5.1.41.4.2 Test procedure The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. PDCCHs indicating new transmissions shall be sent continuously to ensure that the UE would not enter the DRX state. The test consists of three five time periods, with time durations of T1, T2, T3, T4 and T5 respectively. Before the start of T1, the UE is connected to Cell 1 (source PCell) on radio channel 1 but is not aware of Cell 2 (neighbour cell) on radio channel 2. During T1, the UE shall not have any timing information of Cell 2. Before the start of T2, the UE in the measurement control information that event-triggered reporting with Event A3 is configured for neighbour cell (Cell 2), and the UE is configured with the measurement gaps (gap pattern ID \# 0). Starting T2, Cell 2 becomes known to the UE. During T2, the UE shall report Event A3. After receiving the Event A3, the test system shall send a RRC message implying DAPS handover to the UE. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying DAPS handover to Cell 2 (target PCell) is sent to the UE. During T3, the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and shall be able to perform random access to Cell 2. After the RACH procedure is completed, the test system shall send a RRC message to the UE to release Cell 1 (source cell) on radio channel 1. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. During T4, the UE shall perform source cell release. Starting T5, the UE shall stops to send CSI report to the source cell. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.41.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table H.3.1-1 to configure the event-triggered reporting with Event A3. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.41.5-1. T2 starts. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.41.4.3-6 implying DAPS handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC connection reconfiguration message implying DAPS handover to Cell 2 (target PCell) is sent to the UE. At that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.41.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 50 ms from the beginning of time period T3, and during T3 no more than 4 ACK/NACK loss are detected by SS, then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. After the RACH procedure is completed, SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.41.4.3-6 to release Cell 1 (source cell) on radio channel 1. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. At that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T3 to T4 as specified in Table 5.1.41.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If during T4 no more than 4 ACK/NACK loss are detected by SS, the number of successful tests is increased by one.Otherwise the number of failed tests is increased by one. When T4 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T4 to T5 as specified in Table 5.1.41.5-1. T5 starts. The UE shall stop sending CSI reports on Cell1 during T5, if the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise the number of failed tests is increased by one. After T5 expires, cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-18 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 16 and forward. Applicability requires support for Inter-frequency async DAPS handover and FGI bits 5, 13 and 25.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receive a RRC message implying E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. D = T + T + 20 ms Where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is the interruption uncertainty in acquiring the first available PRACH occasion in the new cell. T can be up to 30 ms. During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 6ms (T ). After successful RACH procedure of the target cell, when the UE receives an RRC message implying source cell release command, the UE shall accomplish the release actions specified in TS 38.331 within D . D = T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on target cell. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.7.2.1and A.5.1.42.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10MHz as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in TS 36.508 Annex A figure A.14 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.78a for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set up according to Table 5.1.42.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Message contents are defined in clause 5.1.42.4.3. There are two E-UTRA FDD carriers and one cell on each carrier specified in the test. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test. 5.1.42.4.2 Test procedure The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. PDCCHs indicating new transmissions shall be sent continuously to ensure that the UE would not enter the DRX state. The test consists of five successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2, T3, T4 and T5 respectively. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.42.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-6 implying DAPS handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC connection reconfiguration message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. 10. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 50 ms from the beginning of time period T3, continue with step 11. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one, skip to step 18. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-12 implying source cell release. 12. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. During T4, the UE shall perform source cell release. 13. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE transmits the RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2 less than 21ms from the beginning of time period T4 continues with step 15. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one and skip to step 17. 15. Starting T5 and the UE shall stops to send CSI report to the source cell. 16. If the UE stops to send CSI report to the source cell, the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. 17. Cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the DAPS handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-18 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to TS 36.508 clause 4.6 with the following exceptions: FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test requirement 5.1.42.5 Test requirement Tables 5.1.42.4.1-1, 5.1.42.5-1, and 5.1.42.5-2 define the primary level settings including test tolerances for E-UTRAN FDD FDD Intra-band Inter-frequency async DAPS handover test case. The handover delay D is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T3, to the moment the UE start to transmit the PRACH to Cell 2. The handover delay D test requirement in this case is expressed as: The handover delay D can be expressed as: D = T + T + 20 ms. The handover delay D shall be less than a total of 50 ms in this test case (note: this gives a total of 15 ms for maximum RRC procedure delay plus 15 ms for T ). During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 6ms (T ). The handover delay D is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T4, to the moment the UE start to transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2. The handover delay D test requirement in this case is expressed as: Handover delay D =T + T , where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T = 6 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. The handover delay D shall be less than a total of 21ms in this test case. For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 90\%.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Inter-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Test purpose
Content: To verify the UE’s ability to perform E-UTRAN FDD FDD Inter-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover in RRC_CONNECTED state when an E-UTRAN FDD FDD Inter-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover is commanded by meeting the UE maximum RRC procedure delay and interruption time requirements.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Inter-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 16 and forward. Applicability requires support for Inter-frequency DAPS handover and FGI bits 5, 13 and 25.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Inter-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receive a RRC message implying DAPS handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. D = T + T + 20 ms Where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is the interruption uncertainty in acquiring the first available PRACH occasion in the new cell. T can be up to 30 ms. During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 1ms (T ). After successful RACH procedure of the target cell, when the UE receives an RRC message implying source cell release command, the UE shall accomplish the release actions specified in TS 38.331 within D . D = T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on target cell. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.7.2.1and A.5.1.43.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD FDD Inter-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10MHz as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in TS 36.508 Annex A figure A.14 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.78a for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set up according to Table 5.1.43.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Message contents are defined in clause 5.1.43.4.3. There are two E-UTRA FDD carriers and one cell on each carrier specified in the test. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test. 5.1.43.4.2 Test procedure The test scenario comprises of one E-UTRA FDD cell and one E-UTRA FDD cell on different bands. PDCCHs indicating new transmissions shall be sent continuously to ensure that the UE would not enter the DRX state. The test consists of five successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2, T3, T4 and T5 respectively. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.42.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-6 implying DAPS handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC connection reconfiguration message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. 10. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 50 ms from the beginning of time period T3, continue with step 11. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one, skip to step 18. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-12 implying source cell release. 12. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. During T4, the UE shall perform source cell release. 13. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE transmits the RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2 less than 21ms from the beginning of time period T4 continues with step 15. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one and skip to step 17. 15. Starting T5 and the UE shall stops to send CSI report to the source cell. 16. If the UE stops to send CSI report to the source cell, the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. 17. Cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the DAPS handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-18 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

T = 3 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. The handover delay D shall be less than a total of 18ms in this test case. For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover > Test purpose
Content: To verify the UE’s ability to perform E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover in RRC_CONNECTED state when an E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover is commanded by meeting the UE maximum RRC procedure delay and interruption time requirements.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA TDD UE release 16 and forward. Applicability requires support for Intra frequency DAPS handover.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receive a RRC message implying DAPS handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within handover delay seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. The handover delay can be expressed as: RRC procedure delay + D , where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . D = 35 and is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.1. This gives a total of 50 ms. During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 1ms (T ). After successful RACH procedure of the target cell, when the UE receives an RRC message implying source cell release command, the UE shall accomplish the release actions specified in TS 38.331 within D . D = T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on target cell. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.7.2.1and A.5.1.46.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise source to the UE antenna connectors as shown in TS 36.508 Annex A figure A.20 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.78a for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of five successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2, T3, T4 and T5 respectively. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.42.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-6 implying DAPS handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC connection reconfiguration message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. 10. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 50 ms from the beginning of time period T3, continue with step 11. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one, skip to step 18. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-12 implying source cell release. 12. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. During T4, the UE shall perform source cell release. 13. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE transmits the RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2 less than 21ms from the beginning of time period T4 continues with step 15. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one and skip to step 17. 15. Starting T5 and the UE shall stops to send CSI report to the source cell. 16. If the UE stops to send CSI report to the source cell, the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. 17. Cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the DAPS handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-18 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Intra frequency DAPS handover > Test description > Message contents

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD - FDD Intra frequency conditional handover > Test purpose
Content: To verify the UE’s ability to perform conditional handover in RRC_CONNECTED state when an intra-frequency handover is commanded by meeting the UE maximum RRC procedure delay and interruption time requirements.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD - FDD Intra frequency conditional handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE supporting conditional handover from release 16 and onwards.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD - FDD Intra frequency conditional handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receives a RRC message implying conditional handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. D = T + T + T + T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is the delay uncertainty which is the time from when the UE successfully decodes a conditional handover command until a condition exists at the measurement reference point which will trigger the conditional handover. T is the measurements time stated in clause 5.1.2.6.2 in TS 36.133 . T is the conditional execution preparation time in clause 5.1.2.6.3 in TS 36.133 . T is the interruption time stated in clause 5.1.2.6.4 in TS 36.133 . The measurement time delay T is defined as the time period from the end of T until the UE begins the preparation time for handover execution. The measurement event evaluation delay measured without Time To Trigger (TTT) and L3 filtering shall be less than T identify intradefined in clause 8.1.2.2.1 (FDD) and 8.1.2.2.2 (TDD) for intra-frequency conditional handover or T identify inter defined in clause 8.1.2.3.1 (FDD) and 8.1.2.3.2 (TDD) for inter-frequency conditional handover in TS 36.133 . When TTT or L3 filtering is used or IDC autonomous denial is configured or the UE is performing reception and/or transmission of ProSe Direct Discovery and/or ProSe Direct Communication, or the UE is configured to perform SRS carrier based switching, an additional delay can be expected. If a cell which has been detectable at least for the time period Tidentify_intradefined in clause 8.1.2.2.1. (FDD) and 8.1.2.2.2 (TDD) or T identify inter defined in clause 8.1.2.3.1 (FDD) and 8.1.2.3.2 (TDD) becomes undetectable for a period $ $ 5 seconds and then the cell becomes detectable again and triggers a handover, the measurement time delay shall be less than T or T provided the timing to that cell has not changed more than $ $ 50 Ts and the L3 filter has not been used. When L3 filtering is used or IDC autonomous denial is configured or the UE is performing reception and/or transmission for ProSe Direct Discovery and/or ProSe Direct Communication, or the UE is configured to perform SRS carrier based switching, an additional delay can be expected. Preparation time is the time when the UE prepares the target cell for conditional handover. It begins after measurement time. T is the time needed for preparing the conditional handover to the target cell. T can be up to 10 ms. The interruption time is the time between when the UE completes the preparation time T and the time when the UE starts the transmission of the PRACH to the target cell. For intra-frequency or inter-frequency conditional handover, the interruption time shall be less than T = T + 20 ms Where: T is the interruption uncertainty in acquiring the first available PRACH occasion in the new cell. T can be up to 30 ms. NOTE: The actual value of T shall depend upon the PRACH configuration used in the target cell. In the interruption requirement a cell is known if it has been meeting the relevant cell identification requirement during the last 5 seconds otherwise it is unknown. Relevant cell identification requirements are described in Clause 8.1.2.2.1 (FDD) and 8.1.2.2.2 (TDD) (FDD) and 8.1.2.2.2 (TDD) for intra-frequency conditional handover and Clause 8.1.2.3.1 (FDD) and 8.1.2.3.2 (TDD) for inter-frequency conditional handover. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.1.2.6.and A.5.1.47.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - TDD Inter frequency conditional handover > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to TS 36.508 values 4.6 with the following exceptions: 5.1.50.5 Test requirement Tables 5.1.50.5-1 defines the primary level settings including test tolerances for E-UTRAN TDD-TDD inter frequency conditional handover test case. The handover delay is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T2, to the moment the UE start to transmit the PRACH to Cell 2. The handover delay D test requirement in this case is expressed as: Handover delay D = T + T + T + T + T , where: T = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T = 3840 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.1.2.6.2 in TS 36.133 without T . T = 10 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.1.2.6.3 in TS 36.133 . T = 50 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.1.2.6.4 in TS 36.133 . T + T occurs during T1 as the handover condition becomes satisfied at the start of T2. The test shall verify that there are no interruptions during T1. The UE shall start to transmit the PRACH to Cell 2 less than T + T + T = 3900 ms from the start of T2 and interruption during T2 shall not exceed 50ms. The rate of correct conditional handovers observed during repeated tests shall be at least 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD - TDD Inter frequency conditional handover > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of two successive time periods, with time durations of T1 and T2respectively. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.51.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message including conditionalReconfiguration. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.51.5-1. UE shall execute the conditional handover triggered by Event A3 and send the RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete. 7. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 3900 ms from the beginning of time period T2, then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. 8. Cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the CHO handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-9 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD TDD Intra-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receive a RRC message implying DAPS handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. D = T + T + 20 ms Where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is the interruption uncertainty in acquiring the first available PRACH occasion in the new cell. T can be up to 30 ms. During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 5ms (T ). After successful RACH procedure of the target cell, when the UE receives an RRC message implying source cell release command, the UE shall accomplish the release actions specified in TS 38.331 within D . D = T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on target cell. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.7.2.1and A.5.1.53.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD TDD Intra-band Inter-frequency sync DAPS handover > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise source to the UE antenna connectors as shown in TS 36.508 Annex A figure A.20 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.78a for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set up according to Table 5.1.53.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Message contents are defined in clause 5.1.53.4.3. There is one E-UTRA TDD carrier and two cells specified in the test. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test. 5.1.53.4.2 Test procedure The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. PDCCHs indicating new transmissions shall be sent continuously to ensure that the UE would not enter the DRX state. The test consists of five successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2, T3, T4 and T5 respectively. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.42.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-6 implying DAPS handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC connection reconfiguration message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. 10. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 50 ms from the beginning of time period T3, continue with step 11. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one, skip to step 18. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-12 implying source cell release. 12. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. During T4, the UE shall perform source cell release. 13. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE transmits the RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2 less than 21ms from the beginning of time period T4 continues with step 15. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one and skip to step 17. 15. Starting T5 and the UE shall stops to send CSI report to the source cell. 16. If the UE stops to send CSI report to the source cell, the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. 17. Cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the DAPS handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-18 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise source to the UE antenna connectors as shown in TS 36.508 Annex A figure A.20 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.78a for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set up according to Table 5.1.55.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Message contents are defined in clause 5.1.55.4.3. There are two E-UTRA carriers and one E-UTRA FDD Cell 1 and E-UTRA TDD Cell 2 on each carrier specified in the test. E-UTRA FDD Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD - TDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test scenario comprises of one E-UTRA FDD cell and one E-UTRA TDD cell. PDCCHs indicating new transmissions shall be sent continuously to ensure that the UE would not enter the DRX state. The test consists of five successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2, T3, T4 and T5 respectively. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 5.1.42.5-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event A3. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-6 implying DAPS handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC connection reconfiguration message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.1.42.5-1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. 10. If the UE transmits the uplink PRACH channel to Cell 2 less than 50 ms from the beginning of time period T3, continue with step 11. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one, skip to step 18. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message defined in Table 5.1.42.4.3-12 implying source cell release. 12. The start of T4 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying source cell release is sent to the UE. During T4, the UE shall perform source cell release. 13. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. If the UE transmits the RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2 less than 21ms from the beginning of time period T4 continues with step 15. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one and skip to step 17. 15. Starting T5 and the UE shall stops to send CSI report to the source cell. 16. If the UE stops to send CSI report to the source cell, the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. 17. Cause UE handover back to Cell 1 (if the DAPS handover fails, switch off the UE) or switch off the UE. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set Cell 2 physical cell identity = ((current cell 2 physical cell identity + 1) mod 14 + 2) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-18 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN FDD - TDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to TS 36.508 clause 4.6 with the following exceptions: 5.1.55.5 Test requirement Tables 5.1.55.4.1-1, 5.1.55.5-1, and 5.1.55.5-2 define the primary level settings including test tolerances for E-UTRAN FDD - TDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover test case. The handover delay D is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T3, to the moment the UE start to transmit the PRACH to Cell 2. The handover delay D test requirement in this case is expressed as: The handover delay D can be expressed as: D =TRRC_procedure + Tsearch + TIU + 20ms. The handover delay D shall be less than a total of 65ms in this test case (note: this gives a total of 15 ms for maximum RRC procedure delay plus 30 ms for T ). During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 1ms (T ). The handover delay D is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T4, to the moment the UE start to transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message to Cell 2. The handover delay D test requirement in this case is expressed as: Handover delay D =T + T , where: RRC procedure delay = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T = 1 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. The handover delay D shall be less than a total of 16ms in this test case. For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - FDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover > Test purpose
Content: To verify the UE’s ability to perform E-UTRAN TDD - FDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover in RRC_CONNECTED state when an E-UTRAN TDD - FDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover is commanded by meeting the UE maximum RRC procedure delay and interruption time requirements.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - FDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA UE supporting FDD and TDD UE release 16 and forward. Applicability requires support for Inter-frequency DAPS handover and Feature Group Indicators 5, 25 and 30.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > E-UTRAN Handover > E-UTRAN TDD - FDD inter-band inter-frequency synchronous DAPS handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receive a RRC message implying DAPS handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink PRACH channel within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. D = TRRC_procedure + Tsearch + TIU + 20ms Where: T = 15 ms and is specified in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T = 0 ms in the test as it is assumed as known cell; T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.1. T = 30 ms in the test; T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.1. During D the UE shall be continuously scheduled on Cell 1 and the interruption on Cell 1 shall not exceed 1ms (T ). After successful RACH procedure of the target cell, when the UE receives an RRC message implying source cell release command, the UE shall accomplish the release actions specified in TS 38.331 within D . D = T + T Where: T is the maximum RRC procedure delay to be defined in clause 11.2 in TS 36.331 . T is defined in clause 5.7.2.1.2. During D the UE is allowed an interruption of up to T on target cell. The normative reference for this requirement is TS 36.133 clause 5.7.2.1and A.5.1.56.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN FDD handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receives a RRC message implying handover to UTRAN the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new UTRA uplink DPCCH within D seconds from the end of the last E-UTRAN TTI containing the RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command. Where: D equals the RRC procedure delay, which is 50 ms plus the interruption time stated in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.1.1.2. The interruption time is the time between the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command on the E-UTRAN PDSCH and the time the UE starts transmission on the uplink DPCCH in UTRAN FDD, excluding the RRC procedure delay. The interruption time depends on whether the target cell is known to the UE or not. The target cell is known if it has been measured by the UE during the last 5 seconds otherwise it is unknown. The UE shall always perform a UTRA synchronisation procedure as part of the handover procedure. If the target cell is known the interruption time shall be less than T interrupt1. T interrupt1 = T + T + 50 + 10*F + T ms If the target cell is unknown the interruption time shall be less than T interrupt2. T interrupt2 = T + T + 150 + 10*F + T ms This requirement shall be met, provided that there is one target cell in the MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command. Performance requirements for E-UTRA to UTRA soft handover are not specified. When UE is connected to an E-UTRA cell, UTRA SFN timing measurements are not reported. This implies that the timing of the DPCH of the UTRA target cells in the active set cannot be configured by UTRAN to guarantee that all target cells fall within the UE reception window of T +/- 148 chips. Where: []T is the interruption uncertainty when changing the timing from the E-UTRAN to the new UTRAN cell. T can be up to one UTRA frame (10 ms). []F denotes the maximum number of radio frames within the transmission time intervals of all transport channels that are multiplexed into the same CCTrCH on the UTRA target cell. If HS-PDSCH is configured in the UTRA target cell, F is 4 radio frames. []T is the time required for measuring the downlink DPCCH channel as stated in 3GPP TS 25.214 clause 4.3.1.2. In case higher layers indicate the usage of a post-verification period T = 0 ms. Otherwise T = 40 ms. []T is 0 ms if a single UTRA cell is configured as the handover target, otherwise 20 ms if handover to UTRA with 1, 2 or 3 UTRA carriers with secondary HS-PDSCH is configured. The phase reference is the UTRA primary CPICH. The requirements assume that N312 has the smallest possible value i.e. only one in-sync is required. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.1 and A.5.2.1.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN FDD handover > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and 3GPP TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.22 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.86 (without using the faders) for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set up according to Table 5.2.1.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Message contents are defined in clause 5.2.1.4.3. There is one E-UTRA FDD serving cell and one UTRA FDD cell specified in the test. Cell 1 (E-UTRA FDD cell) is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN FDD handover > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of three successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2 and T3 respectively. At the start of time duration T1, the UE does not have any timing information of Cell 2. Starting T2, Cell 2 becomes detectable and the UE is expected to detect and send a measurement report. Gap pattern configuration with id \#0 as specified in Table 8.1.2.1-1 is configured before T2 begins to enable inter-RAT frequency monitoring. The RRC message implying handover shall be sent to the UE during T2, after the UE has reported Event B2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying handover is sent to the UE. The handover message shall contain cell 2 as the target cell. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table's 5.2.1.5-1 and 5.2.1.5-2. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. The SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table's 5.2.1.5-1 and 5.2.1.5-2. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event B2. SS shall transmit a MobilityFromEUTRACommand message implying handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Tables 5.2.1.5-1 and 5.2.1.5-2. If the UE transmits the UL DPCCH to Cell 2 less than 190 ms from the beginning of time period T3 then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure testes is increased by one. After T3 expires, the UE shall be switched off. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set Cell 2 primary scrambling code = ((current cell 2 primary scrambling code - 50) mod 200 + 100) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-11 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN FDD handover > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to TS 36.508 clause 4.6 and 4.7B with the following exceptions: 5.2.1.5 Test requirement Tables 5.2.1.4.1-1, 5.2.1.5-1 and 5.2.1.5-2 define the primary level settings including test tolerances for E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN FDD handover test. The handover delay is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T3, to the moment the UE start to transmit the UL DPCCH to Cell 2. The handover delay D test requirement in this case is expressed as: Handover delay D = maximum RRC procedure delay + T interrupt1 (note: the target cell is known) T interrupt1= T + T + 50 + 10*F + T ms []T = 10 ms; T can be up to one UTRA frame (10 ms). []F = 4 radio frames; The maximum radio frames within the transmission time intervals to fit into DCCH with 40 ms TTI []T = 40 ms; In case higher layers indicate the usage of a post-verification period T = 0 ms. Otherwise T = 40 ms []T = 0 ms if a single UTRA cell is configured as the handover target. Otherwise T = 20 ms Maximum RRC procedure delay = 50 ms as defined in 3GPP TS 36.331 clause 11.2 The handover delay D shall be less than a total of 190 ms in this test case (note: this gives a total of 50 ms for maximum RRC procedure delay plus 140 ms for T interrupt1 ). For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN TDD - UTRAN FDD handover > Test purpose

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN TDD - UTRAN FDD handover > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one E-UTRAN TDD cell and one neighbour UTRAN FDD cell. The test consists of three successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2 and T3 respectively. During the time T2, Cell 2 becomes detectable and the UE is expected to detect and send a measurement report. The RRC message implying handover shall be sent to the UE during T2, after the UE has reported Event B2. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table's 5.2.2.5-1 and 5.2.2.5-2. UE shall transmit a MeasurementReport message triggered by Event B2. SS shall transmit a MobilityFromEUTRACommand message implying handover to Cell 2. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Table 5.2.2.5-1 and 5.2.2.5-2. If the UE transmits the Uplink DPCCH channel to Cell 2 less than 190 ms from the beginning of time period T3 then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure testes is increased by one. After T3 expires, the UE shall be switched off. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set Cell 2 primary scrambling code = ((current cell 2 primary scrambling code 50) mod 200 + 100) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-11 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - GSM handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 8 and forward that support GSM and inter-RAT PS handover to GERAN. Applicability requires support for FGI bits 9, 15 and 23.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - GSM handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The handover delay given in table 5.2.3.3-1 and interruption time given in table 5.2.3.3-2 requirements for the case where the UE has not synchronised to the GSM cell before receiving the RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command are valid when the signal quality of the GSM cell is sufficient for successful synchronisation with one attempt. If the UE is unable to synchronise to the GSM cell on the first attempt, it shall continue to search for synchronisation information for up to 800 ms duration. If after 800 ms the UE has not synchronised to the GSM cell it shall follow the handover failure procedure specified in 3GPP TS 36.331 . When the UE receives a RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command the UE shall be ready to transmit (as specified in 3GPP TS 45.010 ) on the channel of the new RAT within the value defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.3.2.1 and shown in table 5.2.3.3-1 from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. The UE shall process the RRC procedures for the MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command within 50 ms, which is noted as RRC procedure delay. The interruption time is the time between the end of the TTI containing the RRC command on the E-UTRAN PDSCH and the time the UE starts transmission on the uplink channel in GSM, excluding the RRC procedure delay. The interruption time depends on whether the UE has synchronized to the target GSM cell or not and shall be less than the value defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.3.2.1 and shown in table 5.2.3.3-2. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.3 and A.5.2.3.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - GSM handover > Test description > Initial conditions

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - GSM handover > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of three successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2 and T3 respectively. At the start of time duration T1, the UE may not have any timing information of Cell 2. The RRC message implying handover to Cell 2 shall be sent to the UE during T2, after the UE has reported Event B1. T3 is defined as the end of the last E-UTRAN TTI containing the RRC message implying handover. The requirements are also applicable for a UE not requiring measurement gap, in which case no measurement gap pattern is sent. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table's 5.2.3.5-1 and 5.2.3.5-2. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set a different BSIC on Cell 2, as the previous timing information of Cell 2 is invalid in the UE for the next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-11 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - GSM handover > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to TS 36.508 clause 4.6 with the following exceptions: 5.2.3.5 Test requirement Tables 5.2.3.4.1-1, 5.2.3.5-1 and 5.2.3.5-2 defines the primary level settings including test tolerances for E-UTRAN FDD to GSM handover test case. The handover delay is defined as the time from the beginning of time period T3, to the moment the UE start to send access bursts on the new DCCH to Cell 2. The handover delay T test requirement in this case is expressed as: Handover delay T = handover delay + T offset + T UL Handover delay = 90 ms; this is based on handover delay value as defined in Table 5.2.3.3.-1 T offset = 4.65 ms; GSM timing uncertainty between the time from when the UE is ready to transmit until the start of the next timeslot in GSM 26 multiframe structure T UL = 4.65 ms; the time the UE has to wait in case the next timeslot is an idle frame or a SACCH frame The handover delay T shall be less than a total of 100 ms in this test case (note: this gives a total of 99.29 ms but the test allows 100 ms). For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN TDD - UTRAN TDD handover > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: When the UE receives a RRC message implying E-UTRAN/UTRAN TDD handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink DPCH or the SYNC-UL within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command. The interruption time requirements for an unknown target cell shall apply only if the signal quality of the unknown target cell is sufficient for successful synchronisation with one attempt. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.2 and A.5.2.4.

Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set Cell 2 cell parameter id =(current cell 2 cell parameter id +4) mod 16 for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-11 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Content: To verify the UE's ability to transfer a connection between the UE and E-UTRAN FDD to UTRAN TDD in RRC_CONNECTED state by meeting the UE RRC procedure delay and interruption time requirements.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN TDD handover > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of release 8 and forward E-UTRA FDD UEs that support release 9 and forward UTRA TDD. Applicability requires support for FGI bits 8, and 22.
Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - UTRAN TDD handover > Minimum conformance requirements > 1.28Mcps TDD option
Content: When the UE receives a RRC message implying E-UTRAN/UTRAN TDD handover the UE shall be ready to start the transmission of the new uplink DPCH or the SYNC-UL within D seconds from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command. Where: D equals the RRC procedure delay, which is 50 ms plus the interruption time stated in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.2.2.2. The interruption time is the time between the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command on the E-UTRAN PDSCH and the time the UE starts transmission on the uplink DPCH or the SYNC-UL in UTRAN TDD, excluding the RRC procedure delay. The interruption time depends on whether the target cell is known to the UE or not. The UE shall always perform a UTRA synchronisation procedure as part of the handover procedure. If the target cell has been measured by the UE during the last 5 seconds, the interruption time shall be less than T interrupt1. T = T +T +30*F +20 +10*F ms If the target cell has not been measured by the UE during the last 5 seconds, the interruption time shall be less than T interrupt2. T = T +T +30*F + 180 +10*F ms Where: Equal to 10 ms, the frame timing uncertainty between the old cell and the target cell and the time that can elapse until the appearance of a Beacon channel Equal to 10 ms, the time that can elapse until the appearance of the UL timeslot in the target cell Equal to 1 if SFN decoding is required and equal to 0 otherwise denotes the maximum number of radio frames within the transmission time intervals of all transport channels that are multiplexed into the same CCTrCH. The interruption time requirements for an unknown target cell shall apply only if the signal quality of the unknown target cell is sufficient for successful synchronisation with one attempt. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.2 and A.5.2.5.

Cell 1 is the active cell. SS shall change set cell 2 cell parameter id =(current cell 2 cell parameter id +4) mod 16. T interrupt2 = T + T + 150 + 10*F + T ms This requirement shall be met, provided that there is one target cell in the MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command. When UE is connected to an E-UTRA cell, UTRA SFN timing measurements are not reported. This implies that the timing of the DPCH of the UTRA target cells in the active set cannot be configured by UTRAN to guarantee that all target cells fall within the UE reception window of T +/- 148 chips. Where: []T is the interruption uncertainty when changing the timing from the E-UTRAN to the new UTRAN cell. T can be up to one UTRA frame (10 ms). []F denotes the maximum number of radio frames within the transmission time intervals of all transport channels that are multiplexed into the same CCTrCH on the UTRA target cell. If HS-PDSCH is configured in the UTRA target cell, F is 4 radio frames. []T is the time required for measuring the downlink DPCCH channel as stated in 3GPP TS 25.214 clause 4.3.1.2. In case higher layers indicate the usage of a post-verification period T = 0 ms. Otherwise T = 40 ms. []T is 0 ms if a single UTRA cell is configured as the handover target, otherwise 20 ms if handover to UTRA with 1, 2 or 3 UTRA carriers with secondary HS-PDSCH is configured. The phase reference is the primary CPICH. The requirements assume that N312 has the smallest possible value i.e. only one in-sync is required. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.1 and A.5.2.7.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN FDD - GSM handover: unknown target cell > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of two successive time periods, with time durations of T1 and T2 respectively. At the start of time duration T1, the UE may not have any timing information of Cell 2. A RRC message implying handover shall be sent to the UE during period T1. The start of T2 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying handover is sent to the UE. Starting T2, Cell 2 becomes detectable and the UE receives a RRC handover command from the network. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table's 5.2.8.5-1 and 5.2.8.5-2. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. The neighbour cell shall broadcast its own BSIC, SS shall transmit a MobilityFromEUTRACommand message implying handover to Cell 2. The start of T2 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC MobilityFromEUTRACommand message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 5.2.8.5-1 and 5.2.8.5-2. T2 starts. If the UE sends access bursts on the new DCCH to Cell 2 less than 200 ms from the beginning of time period T2 then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure testes is increased by one. After T2 expires, the UE shall be switched off. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set a different BSIC on Cell 2, as the previous timing information of Cell 2 is invalid in the UE for the next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-7 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%.

Title Path: E-UTRAN RRC_CONNECTED State Mobility > Handover from E-UTRAN to other RATs > E-UTRAN TDD - GSM handover: unknown target cell > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The handover delay given in table 5.2.9.3-1 and interruption time given in table 5.2.9.3-2 requirements for the case where the UE has not synchronised to the GSM cell before receiving the RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command are valid when the signal quality of the GSM cell is sufficient for successful synchronisation with one attempt. If the UE is unable to synchronise to the GSM cell on the first attempt, it shall continue to search for synchronisation information for up to 800 ms duration. If after 800 ms the UE has not synchronised to the GSM cell it shall follow the handover failure procedure specified in 3GPP TS 36.331 . When the UE receives a RRC MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command the UE shall be ready to transmit (as specified in 3GPP TS 45.010 ) on the channel of the new RAT within the value defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.3.2.1 and shown in table 5.2.9.3-1 from the end of the last TTI containing the RRC command. The UE shall process the RRC procedures for the MOBILITY FROM E-UTRA command within 50 ms, which is noted as RRC procedure delay. The interruption time is the time between the end of the TTI containing the RRC command on the E-UTRAN PDSCH and the time the UE starts transmission on the uplink channel in GSM, excluding the RRC procedure delay. The interruption time depends on whether the UE has synchronized to the target GSM cell or not and shall be less than the value defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.3.2.2 and shown in table 5.2.9.3-2. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 5.3.3 and A.5.2.9.

Content: The test consists of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of three successive time periods, with time durations of T1, T2 and T3 respectively. The start of T3 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message implying handover is sent to the UE, at that instant the SS shall switch the power settings from T2 to T3 as specified in Tables 5.3.1.5-1 and 5.3.1.5-2. If the UE starts to transmit the Reverse Control Channel to Cell 2 in less than 127 ms from the beginning of time period T3 then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure testes is increased by one. After T3 expires, the UE shall be switched off. Then ensure the UE is in State 3B according to TS 36.508 clause 4.5.3B. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set a different PN Offset on Cell 2 so that the previous timing information of Cell 2 is invalid in the UE for the next iteration of the test procedure loop.
