The UE shall start to transmit the SYNCH-UL sequence in the UpPTS to Cell 2 less than 650 ms from the beginning of time period T2. The rate of correct RRC connection release redirection to UTRA TDD observed during repeated tests shall be at least 90\%. The time delay can be expressed as: T + T + N + T + T , where: T = 110 ms, which is specified in 3GPP TS 36.133 section 6.3.2.3. T = 500 ms; which is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 section 6.3.2.3. N = 0. It is the total number of target UTRA TDD frequencies included in RedirectedCarrierInfo in "RRCConnectionRelease" message. It can be up to 4 UTRA TDD frequencies. T = 0 ms, UE does not have to read the system information of the UTRAN TDD since all relevant SI is provided to the UE in the "RRCConnectionRelease" message. T = 40ms. This is the additional delay caused by the random access procedure. This gives a total delay of 650 ms. The time delay (T ) shall be less than: T = T + T + T + T The target UTRA FDD cell shall be considered detectable when: CPICH Ec/Io -15 dB, SCH_Ec/Io -15 dB for at least one channel tap and SCH_Ec/Ior is equally divided between primary synchronisation code and secondary synchronisation code. T : It is the RRC procedure for processing the received message "RRCConnectionRelease". It shall be less than 110 ms. T : It is the time to identify the target UTRA FDD cell. It shall be less than 500 ms. T : It is the time required for acquiring all the relevant system information of the target UTRA FDD cell. This time depends upon whether the UE is provided with the relevant system information of the target UTRA FDD cell or not by the E-UTRAN before the RRC connection is released. T : It is the delay caused due to the random access procedure when sending random access to the target UTRA FDD cell. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 6.3.2.1 and A.6.3.1.

Title Path: RRC Connection Mobility Control > Measure the power and timing of the first preamble and it shall not exceed the values specified in clause Tables 6.2.4.5-3 and 6.2.4.5-5. Content: The test comprises of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of two successive time periods, with time duration of T1, and T2 respectively. The "RRCConnectionRelease" message not containing any system information of Cell 2 shall be sent to the UE during period T1 and the start of T2 is the instant when the last TTI containing the RRC message is sent to the UE. Prior to time duration T2, the UE shall not have any timing information of Cell 2. Cell 2 is powered up at the beginning of the T2. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. Set the parameters according to T1 in Table 6.3.9.5-1 and 6.3.9.5-2. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clauses B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionRelease not containing the relevant system information of Cell 2 during period T1. The SS shall start T2 timer when the last TTI containing the RRCConnectionRelease message is sent to UE. When T2 starts, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 6.3.9.5-1 for Cell 1, and Table 6.3.9.5-2 for Cell 2. If the UE transmits the PRACH to Cell 2 less than 1930 ms from the beginning of time period T2 then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. After T2 expires, the UE shall be switched off. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set Cell 2 primary scrambling code = ((current cell 2 primary scrambling code - 50) mod 200 + 100) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Repeat step 2-8 until the confidence level according to Table G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Content: The test comprises of one active cell and one neighbour cell. The test consists of two successive time periods, with time duration of T1, and T2 respectively. The SS shall start T2 timer when the last TTI containing the RRCConnectionRelease message is sent to the UE. When T2 starts, the SS shall switch the power setting from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 6.3.12.5-1 for Cell 1, and Table 6.3.12.5-2 for Cell 2. If the UE transmits the PRACH to Cell 2 less than 1930 ms from the beginning of time period T2 then the number of successful tests are increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. After T2 expires, the UE shall be switched off. Then ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Cell 1 is the active cell. The SS shall set Cell 2 primary scrambling code = ((current cell 2 primary scrambling code - 50) mod 200 + 100) for next iteration of the test procedure loop. Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1.2 and shown in table 7.1.1.3-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX cycle for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. The uplink frame transmission takes place $(N_ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $ before the reception of the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame from the reference cell. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control requirement shall be the downlink timing minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. where: N is 0 $ $ N $ $ 20512 N is 0 for PRACH; $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is the difference between UE transmission timing and the downlink timing immediately after when the last timing advance in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.3 was applied. N $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is not changed until next timing advance is received. N is 0 for frame structure type 1 as defined in 3GPP TS 36.211 clause 8.1.T denotes the basic time unit. The size of various fields in the time domain is expressed as a number of time units T = 1/(15000 x 2048) seconds. When it is not the first transmission in a DRX cycle or there is no DRX cycle, and when it is the transmission for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS transmission, the UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame except when the timing advance in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.3 is applied. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference timing exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T . The reference timing shall be $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $ before the downlink timing. All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be T . The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 7 * $ $ T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be T per 200 ms. Where the maximum autonomous time adjustment step T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1.2 and shown in table 7.1.1.3-2. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1 and A.7.1.1. Both the allowed UE frequency error and the UE time adjustment quantisation can affect the result of the test, and it is not possible to test the UE Transmit Timing Accuracy in isolation from these core requirements. They are therefore taken into account when setting the Test Tolerances and the Test Requirements

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of a single cell. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of Cell 1. The downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed and the changes in UE transmit timing are observed. The transmit timing is verified by the UE transmitting SRS used as a measurement reference facilitating the SS timing estimation. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Set the parameters according to Test 1, Test 2, or Test 3 in Tables 7.1.1.5-1, 7.1.1.5-2 and 7.1.1.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.1.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. The SS adjusts the downlink timing for Cell 1 to a delay of +64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) for $ $3 MHz downlink bandwidth (Test 1, Test 2) and a delay of +128$ $ T (approximately +4 $ $s) for 1.4MHz downlink bandwidth (Test 3) compared to that in step 5. For Test 2, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15 )ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 7 applies for Test 1 and Test 3, but is omitted for Test 2. The test system samples the UE Transmit Timing once per SRS transmission (periodicity 2 subframes). To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one SRS transmission (subframe n) to next (subframe n+2) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.1.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.1.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 1.002s sliding window, with step size 2ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.1.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 198ms sliding window, with step size 2ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offset is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.1.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. In case for Test 1 and Test 3, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.1.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. In case for Test 2, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.1.5-4 For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 1-10 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.1.5-1, 7.1.1.5-2 and 7.1.1.5-3 as appropriate.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 11 that supports Uplink Carrier Aggregation. Applicability requires support for FGI bit 5.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is specified in Table 7.1.2-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX cycle for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control requirement shall be the downlink timing of the reference cell minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The downlink timing is defined as the time when the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame is received from the reference cell. N for PRACH is defined as 0. $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is the difference between UE transmission timing and the Downlink timing immediately after when the last timing advance in clause 7.3 was applied. N for other channels is not changed until next timing advance is received. When it is not the first transmission in a DRX cycle or there is no DRX cycle, and when it is the transmission for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS transmission, the UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame of the reference cell except when the timing advance in clause 7.3 is applied. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference timing exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T . The reference timing shall be $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $ before the downlink timing of the reference cell. All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be T seconds. The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 7*T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be T per 200ms. where the maximum autonomous time adjustment step T is specified in Table 7.1.2-2. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1.2 and A.7.1.3.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and 3GPP TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 20 MHz as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.45. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Cell 1 is PCell on the primary component carrier, Cell 2 is SCell on the secondary component carrier. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power levels set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test. Cell 2 shall be powered OFF.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of two cells, PCell and SCell. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of PCell (Cell 1). The downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed and the changes in UE transmit timing of both PCell and SCell are observed. The transmit timing is verified by the UE transmitting SRS (Sounding Reference Symbols) used as a measurement reference facilitating the SS timing estimation. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Configure SCell according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for all downlink physical channels. The SS shall configure SCell (Cell 2) on the SCC as per TS 36.508 clause 5.2A.4 with UL CA. The SS activates SCC by sending the activation MAC-CE (Refer TS 36.321 , clauses 5.13, 6.1.3.8). Wait for at least 2 seconds (Refer TS 36.133 , clauses 8.3.3.2). Set the parameters according to Test 1 and Test 2 in Tables 7.1.3.5-1, 7.1.3.5-2 and 7.1.3.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. The SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message on Cell 1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell are within the limits specified in Table 7.1.3.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of PCell (Cell 1). The SS adjusts the downlink timing for PCell (Cell 1) to a delay of +64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) compared to that in step 8. For Test 2, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15) ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 10 applies for Test 1, but is omitted for Test 2. The test system samples the UE Transmit Timing once per SRS transmission (periodicity 2 subframes). To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one SRS transmission (subframe n) to next (subframe n+2) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.3.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.3.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 1.002s sliding window, with step size 2ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.3.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 198ms sliding window, with step size 2ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell are within the limits specified in Table 7.1.3.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of PCell (Cell 1). In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell stay within the limits specified in Table 7.1.3.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of PCell (Cell 1). In case for Test 2, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell stay within the limits specified in Table 7.1.3.5-4. For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of PCell (Cell 1) is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 1-13 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.3.5-1, 7.1.3.5-2 and 7.1.3.5-3 as appropriate.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA TDD UE release 11 that supports Uplink Carrier Aggregation. Applicability requires support for FGI bit 5.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is specified in Table 7.1.4.3-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX cycle for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control requirement shall be the downlink timing of the reference cell minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The downlink timing is defined as the time when the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame is received from the reference cell. N for PRACH is defined as 0. $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is the difference between UE transmission timing and the Downlink timing immediately after when the last timing advance in clause 7.3 was applied. N for other channels is not changed until next timing advance is received. When it is not the first transmission in a DRX cycle or there is no DRX cycle, and when it is the transmission for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS transmission, the UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame of the reference cell except when the timing advance in clause 7.3 is applied. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference timing exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T . The reference timing shall be $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $ before the downlink timing of the reference cell. All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be T seconds. The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 7*T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be T per 200ms. where the maximum autonomous time adjustment step T is specified in Table 7.1.4.3-2. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1.2 and A.7.1.4

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of two cells, PCell and SCell. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of PCell (Cell 1). The downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed and the changes in UE transmit timing of both PCell and SCell are observed. The transmit timing is verified by the UE transmitting SRS (Sounding Reference Symbols) used as a measurement reference facilitating the SS timing estimation. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Configure SCell according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for all downlink physical channels. The SS shall configure SCell (Cell 2) on the SCC as per TS 36.508 clause 5.2A.4 with UL CA. The SS activates SCC by sending the activation MAC-CE (Refer TS 36.321 , clauses 5.13, 6.1.3.8). Wait for at least 2 seconds (Refer TS 36.133 , clauses 8.3.3.2). Set the parameters according to Test 1 and Test 2 in Tables 7.1.4.5-1, 7.1.4.5-2 and 7.1.4.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. The SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message on Cell 1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell are 624$ $ T to within the T limits specified in Table 7.1.4.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of PCell (Cell 1). The SS adjusts the downlink timing for PCell (Cell 1) to a delay of +64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) compared to that in step 8. For Test 2, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15) ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 10 applies for Test 1, but is omitted for Test 2. The test system samples the UE Transmit Timing once per SRS transmission (periodicity 10 subframes). To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one SRS transmission (subframe n) to next (subframe n+10) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.4.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.4.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 1.01s sliding window, with step size 10ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.4.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 190ms sliding window, with step size 10ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell are (624 $ $ T ) to within the limits specified in Table 7.1.4.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of PCell (Cell 1). In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell stay at (624 $ $ T ) to within the T limits specified in Table 7.1.4.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of PCell (Cell 1). In case for Test 2, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell stay within the limits specified in Table 7.1.4.5-4. For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 1-13 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.4.5-1, 7.1.4.5-2 and 7.1.4.5-3 as appropriate.

Wait for at least 2 seconds (Refer TS 36.133 , clauses 8.3.3.2). Set the parameters according to Test 1 and Test 2 in Tables 7.1.6.5-1, 7.1.6.5-2 and 7.1.6.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. The SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message on Cell 1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of SCell in sTAG are within the limit specified in Table 7.1.6.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2). The SS adjusts the downlink transmit timing for the activated SCell (Cell 2) to a delay of +64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) compared to that in step 8. For Test 2, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15 )ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 10 applies for Test 1, but is omitted for Test 2. The test system samples the UE Transmit Timing once per SRS transmission (periodicity 2 subframes). To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one SRS transmission (subframe n) to next (subframe n+2) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.6.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.6.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 1.002s sliding window, with step size 2ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.6.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 198ms sliding window, with step size 2ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offsets of SCell are within the limit specified in Table 7.1.6.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2). In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of the SCell in sTAG stay within the limit specified in Table 7.1.6.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2). In case for Test 2, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of the activated SCell (Cell 2) stay within the limit specified in Table 7.1.6.5-4 with respect to the first timing adjustment after downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2) is changed. For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of the activated SCell (Cell 2) is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 1-13 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.6.5-1, 7.1.6.5-2 and 7.1.6.5-3 as appropriate.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell in sTAG > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA TDD UE release 11 and forward that supports Uplink Carrier Aggregation. Applicability requires support for multiple timing advances and FGI bit 5.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell in sTAG > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is specified in Table 7.1.7.3-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX cycle for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control requirement shall be the downlink timing of the reference cell minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The downlink timing is defined as the time when the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame is received from the reference cell. N for PRACH is defined as 0. $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is the difference between UE transmission timing and the Downlink timing immediately after when the last timing advance in clause 7.3 was applied. N for other channels is not changed until next timing advance is received. When it is not the first transmission in a DRX cycle or there is no DRX cycle, and when it is the transmission for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS transmission, the UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame of the reference cell except when the timing advance in clause 7.3 is applied. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference timing exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T , as long as, for the UE configured with a pTAG and an sTAG, the transmission timing difference between TAGs does not exceed the maximum transmission timing difference (i.e., 32.47us) after such adjustment. If the transmission timing difference is bigger than the maximum transmission timing difference (i.e., 32.47us) UE may stop adjustment. The reference timing shall be $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $ before the downlink timing of the reference cell. All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be T seconds. The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 7*T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be T per 200ms. where the maximum autonomous time adjustment step T is specified in Table 7.1.7.3-2. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1.2 and A.7.1.7.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell in sTAG > Test description > Initial conditions

Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz for both PCell and SCell as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.45. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. Cell 1 is PCell on the primary component carrier, Cell 2 is SCell on the secondary component carrier. PCell is in the Primary Timing Advance Group (pTAG) and SCell is in the secondary Timing Advance Group (sTAG). Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power levels set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test. Cell 2 shall be powered OFF.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for SCell in sTAG > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of two cells, PCell and SCell. PCell and SCell are in the Primary Timing Advance Group (pTAG) and the secondary Timing Advance Group (sTAG) respectively. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of SCell (Cell 2) in sTAG. The downlink timing of Cell 2 is changed and the change in UE transmit timing of SCell is observed. The transmit timing is verified by the UE transmitting SRS (Sounding Reference Symbols) used as a measurement reference facilitating the SS timing estimation. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Configure SCell according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for all downlink physical channels. The SS shall configure SCell (Cell 2) on the SCC as per TS 36.508 clause 5.2A.4 with UL CA. The SS activates SCC by sending the activation MAC-CE (Refer TS 36.321 , clauses 5.13, 6.1.3.8). Wait for at least 2 seconds (Refer TS 36.133 , clauses 8.3.3.2). Set the parameters according to Test 1 and Test 2 in Tables 7.1.7.5-1, 7.1.7.5-2 and 7.1.7.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. The SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message on Cell 1. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of SCell in sTAG are 624 $ $ T to within the T limit specified in Table 7.1.7.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2). The SS adjusts the downlink transmit timing for the activated SCell (Cell 2) to a delay of +64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) compared to that in step 8. For Test 2, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15 )ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 10 applies for Test 1, but is omitted for Test 2. The test system samples the UE Transmit Timing once per SRS transmission (periodicity 10 subframes). To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one SRS transmission (subframe n) to next (subframe n+10) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.7.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.7.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 1.01s sliding window, with step size 10ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.7.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 190ms sliding window, with step size 10ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offsets of SCell are (624 $ $ T ) to within the limit specified in Table 7.1.7.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2). In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of the SCell in sTAG stay at (624 $ $ T ) to within the T limit specified in Table 7.1.7.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2). In case for Test 2, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of the activated SCell (Cell 2) stay within the limit specified in Table 7.1.7.5-4 with respect to the first timing adjustment after downlink frame of the activated SCell (Cell 2) is changed. For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of the activated SCell (Cell 2) is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 1-13 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.7.5-1, 7.1.7.5-2 and 7.1.7.5-3 as appropriate.

Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.24.2 and shown in table 7.1.10.3-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX, eDRX_CONN cycle, or the first transmission in a repetition period (R 1) for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. For the 10MHz channel bandwidth, the test sequence shall be carried out in RRC_CONNECTED for both non-DRX (for Test1) and DRX with a cycle length of 80 ms or a cycle length of 640 ms (Tests 2 and, respectively): [ a) ] After a connection is set up with the cell, the test system shall verify that the UE transmit timing offset is within N $ $T $ $ 27$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. In case for Test 2 and Test 3, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.11.5-4. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.13.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 190ms sliding window, with step size 10ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offsets of both PCell and SCell are (624 $ $ T ) to within the limits specified in Table 7.1.13.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell1 (Cell 2) or SCell2 (Cell3). In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of SCell1 and SCell2 stay at (624 $ $ T ) to within the T limits specified in Table 7.1.13.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of the activated SCell1 (Cell 2) or SCell2 (Cell3). In case for Test 2, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offsets of SCell1 and SCell2 stay within the limits specified in Table 7.1.13.5-4. For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of the activated SCell1 (Cell 2) or SCell2 (Cell3) is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 1-13 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.13.5-1, 7.1.13.5-2 and 7.1.13.5-3 as appropriate.

Content: Message contents are according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.6 with the following exceptions: 7.1.13.5 Test requirement Tables 7.1.13.5-1, 7.1.13.5-2 and 7.1.13.5-3 define the primary settings including test tolerances for UE transmit timing accuracy for E-UTRAN TDD test. Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the Cat-M1 UE in CEModeB have the capability to follow the frame timing change of the connected System Simulator. The method used is that the UE initial transmit timing accuracy, the maximum amount of timing change in one adjustment, and the minimum and maximum adjustment rate are within the specified limits based on the requirements.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 13 and forward of UE category M1 that supports CEModeB. Applicability requires support for FGI bit 5.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.1.2 and shown in table 7.1.14.3-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX, eDRX_CONN cycle, or the first transmission in a repetition period (R 1) for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control requirement shall be the downlink timing of the reference cell minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The downlink timing is defined as the time when the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame is received from the reference cell. N for PRACH is defined as 0. $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is the difference between UE transmission timing and the Downlink timing immediately after when the last timing advance in clause 7.3 was applied. N for other channels is not changed until next timing advance is received. When it is not the first transmission in a DRX or eDRX_CONN cycle or there is no DRX or no eDRX_CONN cycle, and when it is the transmission for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS transmission, the UE shall, when no repetitions are configured on the uplink or the repetition period is R=1 , be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame of the serving cell except when the timing advance in clause 7.3 is applied such that the UE transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is specified in Table 7.1.14.3-1. When no repetition period is configured, or the configured repetition period is R=1, all adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be T seconds. The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 7 * T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be T per 200 ms. Where the maximum autonomous time adjustment step T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.24.2 and shown in table 7.1.14.3-2. When a repetition period is configured on the uplink, the UE shall not adjust the uplink transmission timing autonomously during an ongoing repetition period for which R 1. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.24 and A.7.1.14. Both the allowed UE frequency error and the UE time adjustment quantisation can affect the result of the test, and it is not possible to test the UE Transmit Timing Accuracy in isolation from these core requirements. They are therefore taken into account when setting the Test Tolerances and the Test Requirements.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and 3GPP TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.18 (using only main UE Tx/Rx antenna). Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. There is one E-UTRA FDD carrier and one cell specified in the test. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of a single cell. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of Cell 1. The downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed and the changes in UE transmit timing are observed. By measuring the reception of the MPUSCH, the transmit timing accuracy can be measured and the requirements can be verified by the SS. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF-CE with the condition CEModeB according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3AA. Set the parameters according to Test 1, Test 2, or Test 3 in Tables 7.1.14.5-1, 7.1.14.5-2 and 7.1.14.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.14.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. The SS adjusts the downlink timing for Cell 1 to a delay of + 64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) for Test 1 and Test2 and to and a delay of +32$ $ T for Test 3 compared to that in step 5. For Test 2 and Test 3, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15) ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 7 applies for Test 1, but is omitted for Test 2 and Test 3. To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one MPUSCH repetition (in subframe n) to next MPUSCH repetition (in subframe n+2) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.14.5. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.14.5, the SS shall measure the change in MPUSCH repetition timing over a 198 ms sliding window, with step size 2ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offset is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.14.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.14.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. In case for Test 2 and Test 3, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.14.5-4. By measuring the reception of the MPUSCH repetitions, the transmit timing accuracy can be measured and the requirements can be verified. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection, which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF-CE with the condition CEModeB according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3AA. Repeat step 1-10 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.14.5-1, 7.1.14.5-2 and 7.1.14.5-3 as appropriate.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.6 with the condition CEModeB with the following exceptions: 7.1.14.5 Test requirement Tables 7.1.14.5-1, 7.1.14.5-2 and 7.1.14.5-3 define the primary settings including test tolerances for UE transmit timing accuracy for E-UTRAN FDD test. Tables 7.1.14.5-4, 7.1.14.5-5 and 7.1.14.5-6 define the rules for adjustments made to the UE uplink timing include Test Tolerances. For parameters specified in Tables 7.1.14.5-1 and 7.1.14.5-2, the initial transmit timing accuracy, the maximum amount of timing change in one adjustment, the minimum and the maximum adjustment rate shall be within the limits defined in clause 7.1.2. The UE shall not adjust the transmission timing autonomously during an ongoing repetition period. Adjustments can only be done at the end of a last subframe in a repetition period. The following sequence of events shall be used to verify that the requirements are met. For the 10MHz channel bandwidth, the test sequence shall be carried out in RRC_CONNECTED for both non-DRX (for Test1) and DRX with a cycle length of 80 ms or a cycle length of 640 ms (Tests 2 and 3, respectively): [ a) ] After a connection is set up with the cell, the test system shall verify that the UE transmit timing offset is within N $ $T $ $ 51$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. The test system adjusts the downlink transmit timing for the cell by +64$ $T (for Test 1 and Test 2) or +32$ $T (for Test 3) compared to that in (a). The test system shall verify that for Test 1 the adjustment step size and the adjustment rate shall be according to the requirements in clause 7.1.2 until the UE transmit timing offset is within N $ $T $ $ 51$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. Skip this step for Test 2 and Test 3. The test system shall verify that the UE transmit timing offset stays within N $ $T $ $ 51$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. For test 2 and test 3 the UE transmit timing offset shall be verified for the first transmission in the DRX cycle immediately after DL timing adjustment. The UE transmit timing offset shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.14.5-4. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control test requirement shall be the downlink timing minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference cell exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T . All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum adjustment step size T shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.14.5-5 The minimum aggregate adjustment rate is not a meaningful test as the maximum adjustment step of 18T is much greater than the minimum aggregate adjustment rate of 7 * Ts per second, in any 1s period the UE may not make any timing adjustment. A test would therefore be meaningless and this test limit is not applied. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.14.5-6. 7.1.15 E-UTRAN HD-FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeB

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M1 UE in CEModeA > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of a single cell. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of Ncell 1. The downlink timing of Ncell 1 is changed and the changes in UE transmit timing are observed. The transmit timing is verified by the UE transmitting NPUSCH used as a measurement reference facilitating the SS timing estimation. 1. Ensure the UE is in idle State 2A-NB with CP CIoT Optimisation according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 8.1.5. 2. Set the parameters according to Tables 7.1.17.5-1 and 7.1.17.5-2. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. 3. SS sends uplink scheduling information via NPDCCH DCI format N0 for C_RNTI to schedule uplink subframes. The UE shall transmit NPUSCH and the SS shall measure the UE transmit timing offset (n$ $Ts). Using the value of n measured in step 4, the SS calculates the size of the downlink transmit timing for the Ncell 1: if n 0, by +(144 - n )$ $T compared to that in step 4. if n $ $ 0, by -(144 - n )$ $T compared to that in step 4. Before applying the downlink transmit timing adjustment, the SS sends NPDCCH including uplink grant, measures the timing of the resulting NPUSCH, and verifies that it is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.17.5-3 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of NB-IoT cell 1. The SS also records the measured value for use in step 8. Immediately after Step 6, The downlink timing adjustment is performed monotonically in multiple steps of $ $T $ $ 9$ $T per 256ms until the above required total timing change is achieved, during which no grant is transmitted for the UE. Immediately after Step 7, the SS sends NPDCCH including uplink grant for NPUSCH transmission and immediately after receiving NPUSCH the test system repeatedly sends NPDCCH including uplink grant for NPUSCH transmission. The SS samples the UE Transmit Timing once per NPUSCH transmission. The SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size between the first NPUSCH transmission in step 8 and the NPUSCH transmission in step 6 is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.17.5. And using the first NPUSCH transmission in step 8 and subsequent NPUSCH transmissions, the SS shall check the difference in timing between one NPUSCH transmission to the next is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.17.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.17.5, the SS shall measure the change in NPUSCH transmission timing over a 1008ms sliding window, with step size 8ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.17.5, the SS shall measure the change in NPUSCH transmission timing over a 192ms sliding window, with step size 8ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offset is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.17.5-3 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Ncell 1. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.17.5-3 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Ncell 1.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for CE UE in CEModeA > Test requirement
Content: Tables 7.1.21.5-1, 7.1.21.5-2 and 7.1.21.5-3 define the primary settings including test tolerances for E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Cat-M2 UE in CEModeA test. Tables 7.1.21.5-4, 7.1.21.5-5 and 7.1.21.5-6 define the rules for adjustments made to the UE uplink timing include Test Tolerances. For parameters specified in Tables 7.1.21.5-1 and 7.1.21.5-2, the initial transmit timing accuracy, the maximum amount of timing change in one adjustment, the minimum and the maximum adjustment rate shall be within the limits defined in clause 7.26.2 in 3GPP TS 36.133 . The following sequence of events shall be used to verify that the requirements are met. For the 10MHz channel bandwidth, the test sequence shall be carried out in RRC_CONNECTED for both non-DRX (for Test1) and DRX with a cycle length of 80 ms or a cycle length of 640 ms (Tests 2 and 3, respectively): [ a) ] After a connection is set up with the cell, the test system shall verify that the UE transmit timing offset is within N $ $T $ $ 15$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. The test system adjusts the downlink transmit timing for the cell by +64$ $T (for Test 1 and Test 2) or +32$ $T (for Test 3) compared to that in (a). The test system shall verify that for Test 1 the adjustment step size and the adjustment rate shall be according to the requirements in clause 7.26.2 in 3GPP TS 36.133 until the UE transmit timing offset is within N $ $T $ $ 15$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. Skip this step for Test 2 and Test 3. The test system shall verify that the UE transmit timing offset stays within N $ $T $ $ 15$ $T with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of cell 1. For test 2 and test 3 the UE transmit timing offset shall be verified for the first transmission in the DRX cycle immediately after DL timing adjustment. The UE transmit timing offset shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.21.5-4. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control test requirement shall be the downlink timing minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $ The UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference cell exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T . All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum adjustment step size T shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.21.5-5 The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 3.4*T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.21.5-6. 7.1.22 E-UTRAN HD-FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for CE UE in CEModeA
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for CE UE in CEModeA > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the CE UE have the capability to follow the frame timing change of the connected System Simulator. The method used is that the UE initial transmit timing accuracy, the maximum amount of timing change in one adjustment, and the minimum and maximum adjustment rate are within the specified limits based on the requirements.

Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and 3GPP TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.18 (using only main UE Tx/Rx antenna). Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for CE UE in CEModeA > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of a single cell. The transmit timing accuracy is verified related to the downlink frame timing of Cell 1. The downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed and the changes in UE transmit timing are observed. By measuring the reception of the SRS, the transmit timing accuracy can be measured and the requirements can be verified by the SS. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF-CE according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3AA. Set the parameters according to Test 1, Test 2, or Test 3 in Tables 7.1.23.5-1, 7.1.23.5-2 and 7.1.23.5-3 as appropriate. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. The SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset is 624$ $ T to within the limits specified in Table 7.1.23.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. The SS adjusts the downlink timing for Cell 1 to a delay of +64 $ $ T (approximately +2 $ $s) for Test 1 and Test2 and to a delay of +32$ $ T for Test 3 compared to that in step 5. For Test 2 and Test 3, the downlink timing adjustment shall be done at (40 $ $ 15) ms before the next DRX On duration period. Step 7 applies for Test 1, but is omitted for Test 2 and Test 3. The test system samples the UE Transmit Timing once per SRS transmission (periodicity 2 subframes). To check Rule 1, the SS shall check that the maximum time adjustment step size T between one SRS transmission (subframe n) to next (subframe n+2) is within Rule 1 as specified in clause 7.1.23.5. To check that the minimum adjustment rate is within Rule 2 as specified in clause 7.1.1.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 1.002s sliding window, with step size 2ms. To check that the maximum adjustment rate is within Rule 3 as specified in clause 7.1.23.5, the SS shall measure the change in SRS transmission timing over a 198ms sliding window, with step size 2ms. The three rules apply until the UE transmit timing offset is within the limits specified in Table 7.1.23.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. In case for Test 1, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.23.5-4 with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Cell 1. In case for Test 2 and Test 3, the SS shall check that the UE transmit timing offset stays within the limits specified in Table 7.1.23.5-4. For that purpose, the SRS transmission that takes place in the first DRX ON duration after downlink timing of Cell 1 is changed is used. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection, which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF-CE according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3AA. Repeat step 1-10 for each sub-test in Tables 7.1.23.5-1, 7.1.23.5-2 and 7.1.23.5-3 as appropriate.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for CE UE in CEModeA > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA HD-FDD UE Release 14 and forward of UE category M2 and higher, including non-BL/CE UE. Applicability requires support for CEModeB and FGI bit 5.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for CE UE in CEModeA > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The UE initial transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.26.2 and shown in table 7.1.24.3-1. This requirement applies when it is the first transmission in a DRX, eDRX_CONN cycle, or the first transmission in a repetition period (R 1) for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS or it is the PRACH transmission. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control requirement shall be the downlink timing of the reference cell minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The downlink timing is defined as the time when the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame is received from the reference cell. N for PRACH is defined as 0. $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset )$ (in 3GPP TS units) for other channels is the difference between UE transmission timing and the Downlink timing immediately after when the last timing advance in clause 7.3 was applied. N for other channels is not changed until next timing advance is received. When it is not the first transmission in a DRX or eDRX_CONN cycle or there is no DRX or no eDRX_CONN cycle, and when it is the transmission for PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS transmission, the UE shall, when no repetitions are configured on the uplink or the repetition period is R=1, be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame of the reference cell except when the timing advance in clause 7.3 is applied such that the UE transmission timing error shall be less than or equal to $ $T where the timing error limit value T is specified in Table 7.1.24.3-1. When no repetition period is configured, or the configured repetition period is R=1, all adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow these rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be T seconds. The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 7 * T per second. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be T per 200 ms. Where the maximum autonomous time adjustment step T is defined in 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.26.2 and shown in table 7.1.24.3-2. When a repetition period is configured on the uplink, the UE shall not adjust the uplink transmission timing autonomously during an ongoing repetition period for which R 1. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.26 and A.7.1.24. Both the allowed UE frequency error and the UE time adjustment quantisation can affect the result of the test, and it is not possible to test the UE Transmit Timing Accuracy in isolation from these core requirements. They are therefore taken into account when setting the Test Tolerances and the Test Requirements.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN TDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Category NB1 UE In-Band mode under normal coverage > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, TL/VL, TL/VH, TH/VL, TH/VH; as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 8.1.1. Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN TDD - UE Transmit Timing Accuracy Tests for Category NB1 UE In-Band mode under normal coverage > Test requirement
Content: Tables 7.1.27.5-1, 7.1.27.5-2 define the primary settings of Ncell and Cell for UE transmit timing accuracy for TDD Category NB1 UE transmit timing accuracy test. Table 7.1.27.5-3 define the timing error limit with respect to the first detected path (in time) of the corresponding downlink frame of Ncell 1 include Test Tolerances. The UE transmit timing offset shall be within the requirements in Table 7.1.27.5-3. The reference point for the UE initial transmit timing control test requirement shall be the downlink timing minus $(N_ _ +N_ TA offset ) T_ $. The UE shall be capable of changing the transmission timing according to the received downlink frame. When the transmission timing error between the UE and the reference cell exceeds $ $T the UE is required to adjust its timing to within $ $T . All adjustments made to the UE uplink timing shall follow three rules: The maximum amount of the magnitude of the timing change in one adjustment shall be 58.83*T seconds. The minimum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 3.4*TS per 1008ms for carrier frequency under 1 GHz or 0.4*TS per 1008ms for carrier frequency over 1 GHz. The maximum aggregate adjustment rate shall be 59.43*T per 192ms for carrier frequency under 1 GHz or 60.03*T per 192ms for carrier frequency over 1 GHz.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Test purpose
Content: To verify the UE in RRC_CONNECTED state adjusts the timing of its transmissions with accuracy by meeting the E-UTRAN FDD timing advance adjustment requirements in an AWGN model.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Test applicability
Content: This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 8 and forward.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Minimum conformance requirements
Content: The timing advance is initiated from E-UTRAN with MAC message that implies and adjustment of the timing advance according to 3GPP TS 36.321 clause 5.2. The UE shall adjust the timing of its uplink transmission timing at sub-frame n+6 for a timing advancement command received in sub-frame n. The UE shall adjust the timing of its transmission with a relative accuracy better than or equal to $ $4 $ $T seconds to the signalled timing advance value compared to the timing of preceding uplink transmission. The timing advance command is expressed in multiple of 16 $ $ T and is relative to the current uplink timing. In case of random access response, 11-bit timing advance command, T , indicates N values by index values of T = 0, 1, 2,..., 1282, where an amount of the time alignment is given by N = T $ $ 16 according to 3GPP TS 36.213 clause 4.2.3. N is defined in 3GPP TS 36.211 . In other cases, 6-bit timing advance command, T , indicates adjustment of the current N value, N , to the new N value, N , by index values of T = 0, 1, 2,..., 63, where N = N + (T - 31) $ $ 16 according to 3GPP TS 36.213 clause 4.2.3. Adjustment of N value by a positive or a negative amount indicates advancing or delaying the uplink transmission timing by a given amount respectively. For UE timers, the UE shall comply with the timer accuracies according to 3GPP TS 36.133 table 7.2.2-1. The requirements are only related to the actual timing measurements internally in the UE. The normative reference for this requirement is 3GPP TS 36.133 clause 7.3 and A.7.2.1.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Test description > Initial conditions
Content: Test Environment: Normal, as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.1. Frequencies to be tested: According to Annex E table E-1 and 3GPP TS 36.508 clauses 4.4.2 and 4.3.1. Channel Bandwidth to be tested: 10 MHz as defined in 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.3.1. Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.18 for UE with 2Rx RF band and Annex A, Figure A.75 (without using the faders) for 4Rx capable UE without any 2Rx RF bands. The general test parameter settings are set according to Table 7.2.1.4.1-1. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.0. There is one E-UTRA FDD carrier and one cell specified in the test. Cell 1 is the cell used for connection setup with the power level set according to Annex C.0 and C.1 for this test.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of a single cell. The test consists of two successive time periods, with time durations of T1 and T2 respectively. In each time period, timing advance commands are sent to the UE and SRS are sent from the UE and received by the SS. By measuring the reception of the SRS, the transmit timing, and hence the timing advance adjustment accuracy, can be measured. The UE Time Alignment Timer (timeAlignmentTimer IE), defined in 3GPP TS 36.321 clause 5.2, shall be configured so that it does not expire in the duration of the test. Ensure the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Set the parameters according to T1 in Tables 7.2.1.5-1 and 7.2.1.5-2. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. SS shall transmit one message with a timing advance command, T . The timing advance command, T , shall be set to 31 which indicate adjustment of the current N value. The timing advance adjustment during T1 shall be N = 0. The UE shall transmit SRS and adjust its uplink timing at the beginning of sub-frame n+6 for a timing advance command T received in sub-frame n. Sub-frame n is the sub-frame where the UE received the time advance command. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the timing advance command (T ) from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 7.2.1.5-1. SS shall transmit a sequence of messages with timing advance command, T . The timing advance command, T , shall be set to 39 which indicate adjustment of the current N value. The timing advance adjustment during T2 shall be N = 128. The UE shall transmit SRS and adjust its uplink timing at the beginning of sub-frame n+6 for a timing advance command T received in sub-frame n. Sub-frame n is the sub-frame where the UE received the time advance command. The result from the SRS and adjustment of the timing advance in step 9) is used to measure that the UE adjusts the timing of its transmission with a relative accuracy better than or equal to $ $ 4.5 $ $ T to the signalled timing advance value compared to the timing of preceding uplink transmission. If the UE adjust the timing of its transmission within a relative accuracy greater than or equal to $ $ 4.5 $ $ T to the signalled timing advance value compared to the timing of preceding uplink transmission then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. The SS shall transmit RRCConnectionRelease message to release the RRC connection which includes the release of the established radio bearers as well as all radio resources. After the RRC connection release, the SS: - transmits in Cell 1 a Paging message (including PagingRecord with ue-Identity) for the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.5.3A (if the paging fails, switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3), or - switches off and on the UE and ensures the UE is in State 3A-RF according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 7.2A.3. Repeat step 2-13 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.
Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Test description > Message contents
Content: Message contents are according to 3GPP TS 36.508 clause 4.6 with the following exceptions: 7.2.1.5 Test requirement Tables 7.2.1.4.1-1, 7.2.1.5-1 and 7.2.1.5-2 define the primary level settings for E-UTRAN FDD - UE timing advance adjustment accuracy test. The UE shall apply the signalled Timing Advance value to the transmission timing at the designated activation time i.e. 6 sub-frames after the reception of the timing advance command. The UE shall adjust the timing of its transmission with a relative accuracy better than or equal to $ $4.5 $ $ T seconds to the signalled timing advance value compared to the timing of preceding uplink transmission. This requirement includes test tolerances. For the test to pass, the total number of successful tests shall be more than 90\% of the cases with a confidence level of 95\%. 7.2.1_2 E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy for UE category 1bis 7.2.1_2.1 Test purpose Same test purpose as in clause 7.2.1.1 7.2.1_2.2 Test applicability This test applies to all types of E-UTRA FDD UE release 13 and forward of UE category 1bis. 7.2.1_2.3 Minimum conformance requirements Same minimum conformance requirement as 7.2.1.3 7.2.1_2.4 Test description 7.2.1_2.4.1 Initial conditions Same as in Clause 7.2.1.4.1 with the following exceptions: - Connect the SS (node B emulator) and AWGN noise sources to the UE antenna connectors as shown in 3GPP TS 36.508 Annex A, Figure A.18 using only main UE Tx/Rx antenna. 7.2.1_2.4.2 Test procedure Same as in Clause 7.2.1.4.2. 7.2.1_2.4.3 Message contents Same as in Clause 7.2.1.4.3. 7.2.1_2.5 Test requirement Same as in Clause 7.2.1.5.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN TDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of two successive time periods, with time duration of T1 and T2 respectively. In each time period, timing advance commands are sent to the UE and Sounding Reference Signals (SRS), are sent from the UE and received by the test equipment. By measuring the reception of the SRS, the transmit timing, and hence the timing advance adjustment accuracy, can be measured. The UE Time Alignment Timer (timeAlignmentTimer IE), defined in 3GPP TS 36.321 clause 5.2, shall be configured so that it does not expire in the duration of the test. Propagation conditions are set according to Annex B clause B.1.1. T1 starts. SS shall transmit an RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. The UE shall transmit RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete message. SS shall transmit one message with a timing advance command, T . The timing advance command, T , shall be set to 31 which indicate adjustment of the current N value. The timing advance adjustment during T1 shall be N = 0. The UE shall transmit SRS and adjust its uplink timing from the beginning of sub-frame n+6 for a timing advance command T received in sub-frame n. Sub-frame n is the sub-frame where the UE receive the time advance command. When T1 expires, the SS shall switch the timing advance command (T ) from T1 to T2 as specified in Table 7.2.1.5-1. SS shall transmit a sequence of messages with timing advance command, T . The timing advance command, T , shall be set to 39 which indicate adjustment of the current N value. The timing advance adjustment during T2 shall be N = 128. The UE shall transmit SRS and adjust its uplink timing from the beginning of sub-frame n+6 for a timing advance command T received in sub-frame n. Sub-frame n is the sub-frame where the UE receive the time advance command. The timing of the first SRS transmission after sub-frame n+6 and adjustment of the timing advance in step 9) is used to measure that the UE adjusts the timing of its transmission with a relative accuracy better than or equal to $ $ 4.5 $ $ T to the signalled timing advance value compared to the timing of preceding uplink transmission. If the UE adjust the timing of its transmission within a relative accuracy greater than or equal to $ $ 4.5 $ $ T to the signalled timing advance value compared to the timing of preceding uplink transmission then the number of successful tests is increased by one. Otherwise, the number of failure tests is increased by one. Repeat step 2-13 until the confidence level according to Tables G.2.3-1 in Annex G clause G.2 is achieved.

Title Path: Timing and Signalling Characteristic > UE Transmit Timing > E-UTRAN FDD - UE Timing Advance Adjustment Accuracy Test for SCell in sTAG > Test description > Test procedure
Content: The test consists of two cells. The test consists of two successive time periods, with time durations of T1 and T2 respectively.
